title: Verifier‑Augmented LLM for Intent→Configuration Safety (Repaired Preregistration)
research_question: Does integrating a deterministic network verifier into an LLM-driven intent→configuration loop reduce the proportion of unsafe/configurations that fail deterministic validation compared to an LLM-only single-pass baseline on a 300-task synthetic, mixed-vendor NetOps task suite?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H0: Verifier-augmentation does not change the proportion of tasks that achieve a final verifier-pass within the prespecified repair budget versus LLM-only.
H1: Verifier-augmentation (generate→verify→repair loop, ≤2 repairs) produces a ≥30% relative reduction in verifier-failure proportion versus LLM-only on the prespecified task set.
exploratory_questions: Q1: How many repair iterations are typically required to reach verifier-pass?
Q2: Which verifier-assertion categories account for remaining unsafe failures after repairs?
Q3: How sensitive are primary outcomes to one alternate prompt template and to an alternate hosted LLM (subset ablations)?
benchmark_scope: Synthetic task suite of 300 intent→target-state tasks
Three vendor-CLI families: Cisco IOS, Juniper Junos, Arista EOS (synthetic templates)
10 synthetic topologies (30 tasks per topology), CPU-executable deterministic verifiers and reachability simulators
model_scope: Primary: hosted LLM API (single model identifier to be recorded at execution time and logged immutably)
Alternate-ablation: different hosted LLM API (subset of tasks; model identifier to be recorded)
All model calls limited by the capability_manifest maximum planned_model_calls (10000)
transformation_scope: Verifier-guided repair insertion (LLM takes verifier failure assertions as additional prompt context)
primary_estimand: Per-task proportion of tasks with final verifier-pass within the repair budget (binary: pass/fail), averaged across the 300 prespecified tasks (paired comparison between pipelines)
secondary_estimands: Mean model calls per task among tasks that reach verifier-pass
Distribution of remaining failing assertion categories
sampling_plan: Construct 300 confirmatory tasks as follows: generate 10 synthetic topologies (varied sizes and connectivity patterns) via the internal topology generator; for each topology sample 30 intent→target-state tasks distributed equally across three vendor-CLI families (100 tasks per vendor). Use a fixed RNG seed stream for topology and task sampling; if a task triggers an irrecoverable technical failure, replace it (resample) to preserve 300 successful task attempts. Task cluster count = 10 topologies; confirmatory_items = 300; discovery_items = 0.
analysis_plan: Primary confirmatory test: paired McNemar test on per-task final pass/fail (LLM-only vs LLM+Verifier) with two-sided alpha=0.05; report risk difference with 95% Wilson CIs. For model-call counts use paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test; report median and IQR. Provide failure-mode taxonomy counts and descriptive stats. Preserve pairing by running both pipelines on each task. All analysis code, seeds, raw outputs, and verifier logs will be recorded with hashes.
multiplicity_plan: Primary inference is the single prespecified estimand above (McNemar). Secondary endpoints are exploratory; report raw p-values and 95% CIs. For any additional hypothesis tests (post-hoc subgroup tests) label as exploratory and, where multiple exploratory tests are summarized, provide Benjamini–Hochberg FDR-adjusted q-values for interpretive context.
missingness_plan: Per-task timeouts and technical failures: per-task wall-time timeout = 5 minutes; per-model-call timeout = provider default or 120 seconds, whichever is smaller. Retry policy: for transient infrastructure/model API failures, allow up to 2 automatic retries per model call following exponential backoff; if unrecoverable after retries mark as technical failure and resample a replacement task. Tasks with deterministic verifier crashes (parser errors) trigger automatic sanitizer attempts (syntax-normalization routine) up to 1 automatic sanitizer pass; if still failing mark as excluded and resample. All exclusions and replacements logged and counts reported; confirmatory N=300 is maintained by replacement sampling (no manual adjudication).

risk_factors: Possible training-data leakage in hosted LLMs (unknown proprietary corpora)
Task-sampling overlap across phases if seeds are reused incorrectly
Verifier incompleteness (false negatives) leading to optimistic pass counts
detection_procedures: Log and hash all prompts and model outputs; detect verbatim matches between prompts and outputs and flag (deterministic flagging).
Maintain a held-out ground-truth set of 30 tasks with canonical correct configs; run both verifiers and compare to detect verifier false negatives.
Run secondary verifier/simulator on 10% audit sample of passing configs to detect residual unsafe behavior (automated cross-verifier disagreement flags).
item_flagging_rules: If a passing config causes cross-verifier disagreement (primary verifier PASS, secondary verifier FAIL) mark as 'residual_uncertainty' and include in failure-mode breakdown.
If generated config exactly equals any canonical config in the held-out ground-truth set for a different task, flag as potential contamination (deterministic flagging).
contamination_plan.analysis_treatment: Report flagged items counts and treat flagged items as residual uncertainty; primary analysis remains on verifier-pass labels but sensitivity analyses will exclude flagged items and report effect-size differences.
residual_uncertainty: Potential training-data leakage in hosted-models (cannot be fully eliminated)
Verifier false negatives beyond those detected by held-out checks

budget_scenarios.description: Minimal confirmatory run: single hosted LLM, single prompt template, no ablations. Conservative worst-case repair iterations (≤2).
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Model-call total = 300 calls for LLM-only (1 per task) + 900 worst-case for LLM+Verifier (3 per task) = 1,200 calls; this is within the capability_manifest max 10,000 model calls and CPU logging/verification is available.

budget_scenarios.description: Recommended: prespecified confirmatory run plus limited ablations: alternate prompt on 100 disjoint tasks and alternate hosted LLM on another disjoint 100 tasks (both ablations run for both pipelines). Includes verifier-coverage held-out tests and 10% cross-verifier audit.
transformations: LLM+Verifier repair loop (≤2 repairs across all runs)
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Planned calls = primary full-run (300 + 900) = 1,200 + alternate-prompt subset (100 + 300) = 400 + alternate-LLM subset (100 + 300) = 400; total = 2,000 calls. Fits within 10,000-call limit and allows measurement of prompt/model sensitivity while preserving primary confirmatory power.

budget_scenarios.description: Robust/full ablation: run alternate prompt and alternate LLM across the full 300 tasks (max coverage). Includes full secondary-verifier runs on 30% of passing configs.
transformations: intent→config (primary + alternate prompts across all tasks)
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Full-run calls = 1,200 per configuration (primary + L+V) * 3 run variants (primary prompt, alternate prompt, alternate LLM) = 3,600 worst-case. Within 10,000-call limit; higher assurance but higher cost and latency.

power_plan.primary_estimand: Per-task verifier-pass proportion (paired comparison LLM-only vs LLM+Verifier)
power_plan.target_effect: ≥30% relative reduction in verifier-failure proportion under assumed baseline
power_plan.clustering_unit: Task (each task is paired across pipelines); clustering = none beyond per-task pairing; task clusters (topologies) recorded for subgroup analyses.
power_plan.calculation_method: Conservative unpaired two-proportion approximation used for sample-size bound; primary inference will use paired McNemar test. Two-sided alpha=0.05, power target ≥0.8 for detectably large effect; chosen N=300 to provide margin.
assumptions: Conservative assumed baseline verifier-pass rate for LLM-only p0 = 0.50 (no direct numeric baseline in supplied evidence; assumption documented for power calc).
Target relative reduction = 30% → absolute p1 = 0.35 (absolute risk difference = 0.15).

Using unpaired approximate formula yields required n ≈ 170 per arm; with paired design N=170 tasks would be sufficient, so chosen N=300 provides increased power and robustness against assumption misspecification.
power_plan.minimum_detectable_effect_notes: With N=300 and assumptions above, the conservative unpaired approximation implies achieved power ≈96% for absolute risk difference = 0.15 (p0=0.50 → p1=0.35). If baseline verifier-pass is higher (p0>0.50) detectable absolute difference reduces; report sensitivity curves in results.
sensitivity_analyses: Recompute achieved power for alternative baseline rates p0 ∈ {0.30, 0.40, 0.60} and show minimum detectable relative reduction at N=300.
Paired-sample exact-power approximation reported post-hoc using observed discordant-pair counts.

semantic_equivalence_checks: Primary deterministic verifier assertions (syntax + safety + reachability checks) on each generated config
Secondary reachability simulator on 10% audit sample of passing configs (cross-verifier check)
Unit tests on a held-out canonical set of 30 tasks with known correct configs (semantic equivalence expectation)
automatic_rejection_rules: If primary verifier fails to parse config => run automatic syntax-normalizer; if still unparsable => automatic exclusion and replacement (no human intervention).
If primary verifier returns any safety assertion FAIL => automatically request LLM repair with verifier feedback (up to 2 repair iterations).
If after repair budget the config still fails => mark final status = FAIL (confirmatory count recorded).
transformation_validation.audit_sample_policy: Run secondary verifier/simulator on 10% of passing configs (random deterministic seed) and on all held-out canonical 30 tasks; any cross-verifier disagreements are flagged and included in residual uncertainty analysis.
transformation_validation.mapping_validation: 30 held-out canonical tasks with authoritative configs (generated by deterministic templates) used to measure mapping correctness and to estimate primary verifier false-negative modes; report per-assertion-type coverage.
residual_risks: Verifier false negatives beyond held-out detection (conservative interpretation of passes required).
Semantic-liveness issues not modeled by deterministic reachability checks (e.g., device-specific runtime behaviors).

remaining_noncritical_uncertainties: External validity: representativeness of synthetic topologies and synthetic vendor-CLI templates for all production networks.
Hosted LLM training-data leakage (unknown proprietary corpora) cannot be fully excluded; treated as residual uncertainty and flagged when detected.
Deterministic verifier incompleteness (false negatives) despite held-out testing; impacts interpretation of verifier-pass as a proxy for operational safety.
Model nondeterminism and provider-internal updates during the run; mitigated by immutable logging of model identifier and response hashes but not fully eliminable for hosted services.
